The statement-of-reasons branches shift the relevant day (s 33(4)(b)-(c)) — confirm which branch applies to the lawyer-supplied notification facts.

The tribunal may extend the period under s 61, even after it has passed (s 61(2)), but not where the extension would cause prejudice or detriment not remediable by an appropriate order for costs or damages (s 61(3)).

The Royal Queensland Show holiday (Wednesday 12 August 2026; Wednesday 11 August 2027) applies in the Brisbane area only and is included because the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal registry sits at Brisbane; every other local government district has its own appointed show holiday (97 districts in 2026), none of which is included — confirm registry-location holidays before relying on a business-day computation.
Local show holidays for districts outside Brisbane had not been published for 2027 at the checked date.
Christmas Eve is a part-day public holiday (6pm to midnight) and is not included as a non-business day.
Anzac Day is substituted only when 25 April falls on a Sunday: 2026 falls on a Saturday with no substitute; 2027 is observed on Monday 26 April as published.

prompt: Our client was notified of a Queensland reviewable decision on 26 November 2026. When is the QCAT review application due?

key.label: Application to review a reviewable decision (general period, subject to the enabling Act)
key.citation: Queensland Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2009 (Qld) s 33(3)
key.trigger: The relevant day (s 33(4)): the day the applicant is notified of the decision, or where a written statement of reasons was sought under s 158 or ordered under s 159, the earlier of the day the statement is given and the day it was required to be given
key.disclaimer: Candidate date only. The responsible lawyer must confirm every date before reliance. This tool is not a diary, court-list or practice-management system.
